text.p: Privatised Egyptian fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial (EFI) was started with a "strong buy" rating by London-based stockbrokers T. Hoare and Co., the brokerage firm said on Monday.
Analysts said they based their recommendation on:

-- EFI's expansion plans, which will make it the world's largest producer of Single Super Phosphate fertiliser by 1999. These include a new fertiliser plant which will begin working this year and a new product line to start in 1999.
-- The firm currently has 70 percent of the local market, and land reclamation projects, including the giant New Valley scheme, are set to increase that share.

T. Hoare forecast EFI's earnings per share would rise in calendar 1997 to 14.32 pounds ($4.22) from 7.70 in the 12-month period July 1995-June 1996. The firm has moved the start of its financial year to January 1 from July 1.
The Egyptian state sold 65 percent of EFI's total 3.25 million shares to private investors last year.

T. Hoare said EFI earned 34 million pounds in the nine-month period July 96-March 97. It also forecast EFI's operating profits would rise in calendar 1997 to 44.5 million from 31.5 million in the old financial year 1995/6.

Exports, which make up 39 percent of EFI's business, are expected to grow in 1996/7 by 35 percent, the analysts said. They said EFI's low costs gave it the competitive edge over phosphoric fertiliser producers in China, India and Australia.
